          Plymouth Argyle Women beaten away to bottom-of-the-table rivals

          There was a 4-1 defeat for the Pilgrims at Cheltenham Town in the FAWNL Southern Premier Division

          Comments0
          Sport
          Lexie Sanders
          10:38, 12 Oct 2026
          Listen to audio version of this article
          Sponsored by
          0:00 / 4:39
          Instaread

          Plymouth Argyle Women were beaten 4-1 away to Cheltenham Town in the FAWNL Southern Premier Division, with a series of key penalty decisions proving pivotal in a frustrating afternoon for the visitors.

          ‌

          After Charlotte Salisbury-Williams opened the scoring, Laura Curnock equalised for Argyle from the penalty spot following an incident in which Aliyat Lambe had her hair pulled inside the box.

          ‌

          However, Argyle's reprieve was short-lived, as Cheltenham were awarded a contentious penalty of their own just minutes later, with the decision changed from a free-kick to a spot-kick following a discussion between the referee and his assistant.

          ‌

          Emily Owen converted to restore Cheltenham's lead before the break, then scored another penalty early in the second half to put the hosts in control. Chloe Snook added a fourth just after the hour mark as Argyle were left with too much to do.

          Argyle made a positive start and almost took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes. Shana Dolbel’s header struck the crossbar following a pinpoint delivery from Farrah Ambrose, before Curnock’s follow-up header was saved by Chloe Jones.

          Kiesha Walker also produced an important defensive challenge to deny Leonie Joyce a clear sight of goal as both sides looked to establish themselves in the contest.

          ‌

          However, Cheltenham broke the deadlock in the 15th minute when Salisbury-Williams found the top corner with a looping effort from outside the box.

          The hosts continued to threaten, but Argyle remained in the game. Dolbel looked to create an opening with some clever footwork inside the penalty area, although her eventual effort drifted wide.

          At the other end, goalkeeper Liv Giles came out quickly to claim Snook’s cross and prevent Joyce from connecting with a header.

          ‌

          Argyle’s persistence was rewarded in the 38th minute when they were awarded a penalty after Lambe had her hair pulled inside the box and Curnock stepped up and confidently converted from the spot.

          The visitors’ celebrations were short-lived, however, as Cheltenham regained the lead just six minutes later. Following a contentious decision that initially appeared to be a free-kick outside the area, the referee consulted his assistant and awarded a penalty instead and Owen made no mistake from the spot to restore the hosts’ advantage at 2-1.

          There was still time for Dolbel to strike the crossbar for a second time, this time with an effort following a cross, as Argyle headed into the interval trailing after a chaotic opening 45 minutes.

          ‌

          Argyle’s task became more difficult just six minutes after the restart when Cheltenham were awarded another penalty and Owen converted from 12 yards to extend the hosts’ lead to 3-1.

          Giles then produced an excellent save to deny Joyce, before Lambe recovered to block the follow-up effort and force a corner.

          ‌

          Argyle attempted to respond, with Lambe testing Jones with a half-volley from Walker’s free-kick. However, Cheltenham struck again in the 60th minute when Joyce threaded a pass through to Snook, who finished past Giles from the edge of the area to make it 4-1.

          Dolbel continued to search for a way back into the contest, forcing Jones into a save with a long-range strike before Curnock sent the rebound wide. Argyle also won a free-kick on the edge of the box, but could not turn the opportunity into another goal.

          Cheltenham threatened to add to their advantage when Amelie Curtis struck the post with a long-range effort, while both sides made changes during the closing stages.

          ‌

          Argyle introduced Phoebe Bettey for Khloe Reed in the 81st minute, but the visitors were unable to find a late consolation as the hosts secured the three points.

          Cheltenham moved up to 10th position in the 12-team Southern Premier Division after their first win of the season, while Argyle remained bottom after a seventh successive defeat. They are back in action at Home Park this Sunday against third-placed AFC Bournemouth.

          CHELTENHAM: Chloe Jones, Charlotte Salisbury-Williams (Evie Murphy 61 mins), Courtney Jones (Casi Evans 56 mins), Amelie Curtis (Keira O’keefe 76 mins), Leonie Joyce (Georgia Galley 71 mins), Libby Bell (Kaitlyn Hicks-Kenward 61 mins), Lilly Wellesley-Davies, Emily Owen, Alex Hall, Chloe Snook, Ruby Day. Unused subs: Shurima Vine, Darcy Fortner

          Article continues below

          ARGYLE: Liv Giles, Aliyat Lambe, Ellie M Bishop, Laura Curnock, Shana Dolbel, Kiesha Walker, Kennedy Garside, Farrah Ambrose, Brooklyn Brothers, Ciara Magee (Chloe Ingrouille 43 mins), Khloe Reed (Phoebe Bettey 81 mins). Unused subs:Saskia Worrall, Ellie J Bishop.
